solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Following delay man makes US city

blocks.note: f. is the standard abbreviation for 'following', as in page references
a lag is a delay
to man a desk is to staff it

explanation.surface: Someone moves to an American city after a hold-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as a noun but works as a verb: to man a post is to staff it. The city is in Arizona.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagstaff is a city in northern Arizona, so it is an example of a place in the States.

clue.text: Surface — the last labelled on an icosahedron?

blocks.note: an icosahedron is a solid with twenty flat faces
label twenty faces A to T in order and the last one carries T, the twentieth letter

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about which label ends up on the final side of a twenty-faced die.
explanation.walkthrough: The icosahedron has twenty faces; lettered in order, the last is face T, which reads as FACET.
explanation.definitionFit: A facet is one flat plane cut on a gem or solid, so it is a kind of outer plane.

clue.text: Previously referred to a course warning delivered?

blocks.note: kept as it is
'Fore!' is the shout a golfer gives on the course to warn of a flying ball
a line delivered is a line said

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a golfer's warning shout was mentioned earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The course is a golf course, not a meal or a lesson; the warning shouted there is FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal documents use aforesaid for anything already mentioned earlier in the same text, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Senior officers desert rising celebrity

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read from the bottom upward

blocks.note: supers are police superintendents
to rat is to desert, as a rat leaves a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Top police officers abandon a colleague whose fame is growing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' is a verb, not sand: to rat on someone is to desert them. 'Rising' turns it over in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A superstar is an extremely famous performer, the top grade of famous person.

clue.text: Outcome for Hook is barely anything

definitions.note: a cryptic hint read literally: Captain Hook's fate

blocks.note: Captain Hook's end in Peter Pan: he falls from his ship into the sea
the idiom for an amount too tiny to matter

explanation.walkthrough: In Peter Pan, Captain Hook ends by falling from his ship into the sea and the waiting crocodile: literally a drop into the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes an amount so small compared with what is needed that it makes no difference.

clue.text: At sea, meet storm fronts everywhere

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A sailor warns that weather systems will close in on the ship from all sides.
explanation.walkthrough: The nautical surface sits right on top of a nautical answer, which makes the anagram hard to separate from the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The stem is a ship's bow and the stern its back end, so the phrase covers the whole thing, thoroughly throughout.

clue.text: By the sound of it, remained sober

indicators.note: we are told to judge by what is heard, not by the spelling

blocks.note: remained is past tense of stay

explanation.surface: Someone apparently stayed off the drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sober' looks like it means not drunk, which fits 'remained'; it is the definition, meaning serious and dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Staid and sober both describe a serious, restrained, rather dull manner, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Small and large diamonds fade

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
L is the size abbreviation for large
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Gems of every size lose their sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fade' reads as a verb about diamonds losing lustre; it is a golf noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf both are shots that curve away to the side; a slice is the stronger, unwanted version of that curve.

clue.text: Protracted answer leads to a more advanced state

indicators.note: whatever leads goes in front of the rest of the wordplay

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer, as in Q and A
protracted means drawn out, long

explanation.surface: A drawn-out reply moves a discussion forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads to' looks like a single link phrase; split it, with 'leads' placing the A first.
explanation.definitionFit: When work is well along or moves along, it has progressed further, a sense of the adverb meaning onward.

clue.text: One ruminating about southern Ilium — Shiva?

indicators.note: about means around, so one thing is wrapped round another

blocks.note: deer are ruminants, chewing the cud
S is the abbreviation for southern
Ilium is the Latin name for Troy

explanation.surface: A thinker muses on the ancient city and a Hindu god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruminating' suggests pondering; it is literal cud-chewing, making the ruminant a deer.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu tradition Shiva is the god of destruction within the trinity, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Egg beater or another kitchen utensil

blocks.note: slang for a helicopter, whose rotor whirls like a whisk
a cleaver or gadget for cutting food

explanation.surface: A whisk, or some other gadget from the cook's drawer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egg beater' is not a whisk here but slang for a helicopter, whose rotor churns like one; so the 'another kitchen utensil' is the real cooking sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopper is informal for a helicopter, also nicknamed an eggbeater, and names a cleaver or chopping gadget used by cooks.

clue.text: Blood group negative involves nothing sinister

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one piece enfolds another

blocks.note: O is one of the ABO blood groups
minus means negative
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A worrying blood test result that turns out to show nothing bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blood group negative' reads as one medical phrase, O negative; split it into O then MINUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something threatening that suggests harm is coming, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: The short temper of people in general

indicators.note: something short is missing its end

blocks.note: kept as it is
temper is IRE, cut short

explanation.surface: A remark on how quickly everyone loses their cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The short temper' reads as one phrase; it splits as THE plus a shortened IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun can refer to unspecified folk generally, as in 'they say', meaning belonging to them.

clue.text: One who assists eating English fare

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside

blocks.note: in team sports, an assist is a pass that sets up a score
Eng. is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A helper tucks into a traditional English meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' looks like food after 'eating'; it is the person who pays to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi driver's fare is the customer being carried, a paying traveller in a vehicle.

clue.text: Skill of service in court

indicators.note: one thing placed inside another

blocks.note: Ct is the abbreviation for court
the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: The art of serving at tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Service and court point to a tennis match; the service is an armed service, the Royal Air Force.
explanation.definitionFit: Craft means expertise in making or doing something by hand, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Legion to become more insignificant?

definitions.note: a cryptic reading: two words, COUNT LESS

blocks.note: an adjective here: too many to number
read as two words: to matter less

explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like a noun (a Roman army) but is the adjective, as in 'their numbers are legion'. The second half reads as COUNT LESS, matter less.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means too many to number, so it is a synonym for innumerable.

clue.text: Perforce, thoroughly fulfil Baker’s role in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so the words are to be heard

blocks.note: a baker's job is to knead dough, and doing it thoroughly is to knead fully

explanation.surface: An actor at an audition must commit completely to playing the part of Baker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' suggests an actor trying for a role; here it means a hearing. The baker's role is to knead.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old word meaning by necessity, and needfully is its archaic equivalent, a synonym.

clue.text: Recorder reformed Fleet gaol

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a new shape

blocks.note: nine letters of fodder

explanation.surface: A court clerk notes that the old debtors' prison has been improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' looks like a scribe or a judge; it is the woodwind instrument. The Fleet was a famous London prison; gaol is British for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A flageolet is a small wooden flute blown from the end, a close cousin of the school instrument.

clue.text: Double volume in hurry to become a thousand

indicators.note: one thing turns into another, so a letter is swapped for a new one

blocks.note: 'look alive!' is an order to hurry up
V is the symbol for volume
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: An instruction to double the amount quickly until it reaches a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside LOOK ALIVE, the V gives way to K.
explanation.definitionFit: A double is a person who closely resembles someone else, exactly what a celebrity stand-in is.

clue.text: Playing duet with horns, possibly aimed too low

indicators.note: musicians playing rearrange the notes, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: fodder
more fodder, joined by 'with'

explanation.surface: Two brass players in a duet may have pitched their notes flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'aimed too low' sound like a pitch problem; it is a shot falling short.
explanation.definitionFit: An undershot target is one where the shot fell short of it, landing before the mark.

clue.text: Henry leaves some time in the morning for liaison

indicators.note: what leaves is gone, so a letter departs

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
an hour in the a.m.

explanation.surface: Henry slips out early one morning to meet a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is not a lover here but the unit of inductance; its H leaves AM HOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: An amour is a secret love affair, the French word used in English for a romantic intrigue.

clue.text: Persistent cautions deployed involving ecstasy

indicators.note: troops deployed are spread out into new positions
to involve is to take in, so something is included

blocks.note: fodder
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Repeated police warnings about drug use keep being issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cautions' looks like the police kind; it is just letters to shuffle, with E (ecstasy) put among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenacious describes someone who holds on and will not give up, which is persistence.

clue.text: Miles performing soaring finale

indicators.note: in a down clue, soaring means going upward, so read bottom to top

blocks.note: a show that is on is being performed
a finale is the end

explanation.surface: A trumpet solo by Miles Davis climbs to its climax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miles' looks like the jazz trumpeter; it is the intensifier in 'miles better'.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Miles better' and 'no end better' both mean far or hugely better, interchangeable intensifying idioms.

clue.text: Sentimental, having conversely upset companion

indicators.note: conversely is the other way round, and upset tips it over, so letters swap direction

blocks.note: corny means mawkishly sentimental

explanation.surface: A soppy person who has upset a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Not the whole word turns over, only a two-letter run in its middle, which happens to spell the little word 'or' — a nod to 'conversely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crony is a close friend or pal, often used of a long-standing associate.

clue.text: Faithful without pretence

blocks.note: ex means without, as in 'ex dividend'
putting on an act is a pretence

explanation.surface: Loyal, and without any faking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without pretence' reads as a description of sincerity; it gives EX then ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: A faithful copy or translation is one that is accurate and true to its original in detail.

clue.text: Power to secure the darts matches in successive locations

indicators.note: each word gives up the letter one place further along than the word before

blocks.note: first letter
second letter
third letter
fourth letter
fifth letter

explanation.surface: Someone has the clout to win the darts fixtures at a run of venues.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the 1st letter of 'to', the 2nd of 'secure', the 3rd of 'the', the 4th of 'darts' and the 5th of 'matches'.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real force to be enforced, so the plural noun means effective strength.

clue.text: Sight, or what may adversely affect it

definitions.note: a cryptic reading: EYE SORE, a sore eye that harms vision

blocks.note: as in 'you look a sight': something ugly to look at
read as two words: a sore eye harms vision

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sight' looks like vision, which the second half plays on; but it is the other sense, as in 'you look a sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a sight means it is ugly to look at, exactly what an ugly building is called.

clue.text: With stealth, some regressive amoebae kill, eerily

definitions.note: a phrase used as an adjective, 'with stealth' describing a creature

indicators.note: some means only a part of the words that follow
regressive means going backward, so read right to left

blocks.note: the run of letters from the end of the first word into the start of the third

explanation.surface: A microscopic predator creeps up on its prey in a spooky way.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'amoebae kill, eerily' and has to be read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels move sinuously and slip silently through water, so moving like one suggests a sly, slippery stealth.

clue.text: Alas, report 550 cracks

indicators.note: to crack something is to break into it, so one piece gets inside another

blocks.note: to report is to say
D is 500 and L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A news bulletin regrets that hundreds of fractures were found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' looks like a noun; it is a verb, the Roman numerals breaking into SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are words of regret used to introduce unwelcome news, as interjection and sentence adverb.

clue.text: Finally down, wearing the tie, dressed for big birthday?

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the next word
to dress is to arrange, as a window is dressed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the last letter of the word
in means wearing, as in 'in a dress'
fodder

explanation.surface: Someone puts on a tie and dresses up for a milestone birthday party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wearing' looks like part of the dressing-up picture; it simply gives IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaching ninety is a milestone celebration, and the ordinal names that particular anniversary; the question mark flags an example.
